interest: Shows Japan's wartime food crisis (1941-43): commodity shortages, Allied blockade effects, and Swedish vitamin relief via the Gripsholm.
overview: File 894.5018 (May 1941-Jan 1943) documents Japan's worsening food crisis, from civilian rationing and regional shortages to wartime mobilization, British embargoes on oils, OSS salt-supply analysis, and Swedish vitamin shipments via the exchange ship Gripsholm amid Allied blockade.

people.name: Ernest F. Penrose
people.role: Economic Advisor to the U.S. Ambassador to Great Britain

people.name: William D. Leahy
people.role: Admiral, U.S. Navy / Chief of Staff to the Commander in Chief

subfiles.about: Consul Samuel Sokobin reports on the local meat shortage in Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Telegram: Consul Sokobin at Kobe reports an emerging meat shortage, sent to State's Commercial Affairs and Far Eastern Affairs divisions.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Sokobin (Kobe) on Meat Shortage
subfiles.to: Division of Commercial Affairs and Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Chase Kimball requests current information concerning food rationing systems in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Chase Kimball asks the Division of Far Eastern Affairs for current information on food rationing in Japan.
subfiles.title: Inquiry from Chase Kimball regarding Food Rationing in Japan

subfiles.about: The Tokyo Embassy furnishes available information on food rationing in Japan in response to an inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 142: the Tokyo Embassy furnishes data on Japanese food rationing in response to Chase Kimball's inquiry.
subfiles.title: Despatch #142 from Tokyo Embassy furnishing Information on Food Rationing
subfiles.to: Chase Kimball and Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports on the distribution of foodstuffs in Hyogo Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 759: Grew reports on the distribution of foodstuffs in Hyogo Prefecture.
subfiles.title: Telegram #759 from Grew (Tokyo) on Distribution of Foodstuffs in Hyogo Prefecture
subfiles.to: Division of Commercial Affairs and Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Ambassador Grew reports on Japanese representations to the British Ambassador concerning British embargoes on copra exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 792: Grew relays Japan's protest to Britain over its copra embargo, citing severe domestic shortages of vegetable fats and oils.
subfiles.title: Telegram #792 from Grew (Tokyo) on Japanese Representations regarding Copra Embargo
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Division of Commercial Affairs, and Division of European Affairs

subfiles.about: Quotes a message sent to London by the British Ambassador in Tokyo concerning Japan's acute shortage of food oil.
subfiles.summary: Telegram quotes a May 1941 British Ambassador's message on Japan's worsening food oil shortage, following earlier reports on the copra embargo.
subfiles.title: Telegram quoting British Ambassador's Message on Shortage of Food Oil

subfiles.about: The Department of Justice transmits a statement by Lillian Konoye concerning food conditions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Justice Department forwards Lillian Konoye's statement on food conditions in Japan to State's Far Eastern Affairs division.
subfiles.title: Justice Department Transmission of Lillian Konoye's Statement on Food Conditions
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Foreign Activity Correlation

subfiles.about: Transmits an assessment from the British Enemy Resources Department and comments by E. F. Penrose on Japan's 1942 food position.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 270: London transmits a British Enemy Resources Department assessment of Japan's 1942 food position, with commentary by economic adviser E. F. Penrose.
subfiles.title: Telegram #270 from Winant (London) on Japan's Food Position in 1942
subfiles.to: Division of Commercial Affairs and Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to Economic Warfare Intelligence Series No. 124 regarding the effects of the Pacific War on Far Eastern food supplies.
subfiles.summary: Indexes an April 1942 British despatch on the Pacific War's effects on Japanese and Allied food supplies.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Somerville Despatch #3418 on War Effects on Far East Food Supplies

subfiles.about: Transmits OSS Situation Report No. 7 analyzing the strategic importance of salt in the Sino-Japanese struggle.
subfiles.summary: OSS Situation Report No. 7 (June 1942) analyzes salt production, supply routes, and dietary and industrial needs in East Asia, for Allied economic warfare planning.
subfiles.title: Office of Strategic Services Situation Report #7 on the Importance of Salt

subfiles.about: General resume by Ambassador Grew on the foodstuffs situation in Japan proper from December 1941 to April 1942.
subfiles.summary: Despatch from Grew surveys Japan's food situation from December 1941 to April 1942, assessing how wartime isolation affected domestic food reserves and distribution.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Grew on Foodstuffs Situation in Japan (Dec 1941 - Apr 1942)
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Division of Public Affairs/Historical

subfiles.about: The War Department transmits a military intelligence summary of Japan's foodstuff position.
subfiles.summary: War Department memo by Truman W. Martin assesses Japan's overall foodstuff position and its vulnerability to economic interdiction.
subfiles.title: War Department Memorandum by Truman W. Martin on Japan's Foodstuff Position
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence, Far Eastern Affairs, and Historical Division

subfiles.about: Cross-reference regarding a communication informing the Office of Economic Warfare of severe food and vitamin deficiencies in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Indexes an August 1942 note to the Office of Economic Warfare on Japan's worsening food pinch and vitamin-deficient diet.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Letter to Office of Economic Warfare on Vitamin and Medicine Scarcity

subfiles.about: Cross-reference concerning an OEW letter noting armed forces interest in Japanese food and medicine shortages.
subfiles.summary: Indexes a September 1942 OEW letter calling the August report on Japanese food and medicine scarcity important for intelligence.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Office of Economic Warfare Letter on Food and Medicine Scarcity

subfiles.about: Cross-reference regarding a Swedish Legation request to transport 1,000 tons of vitamins and medicines to Tokyo aboard the Gripsholm.
subfiles.summary: Indexes an August 1942 Bern telegram on Sweden's request to ship 1,000 tons of vitamins to Tokyo via the Gripsholm.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Telegram #7190 from Harrison on Swedish Shipment of Vitamins via Gripsholm

subfiles.about: Minister Harrison reports German press accounts stating that Japanese authorities granted additional monthly rations to Germans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 8189: Harrison reports German press coverage that Japan agreed to give German nationals in Japan extra monthly food rations.
subfiles.title: Telegram #8189 from Harrison (Bern) on Additional Rations for Germans in Japan
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Communications and Records, and European Affairs

subfiles.about: Minister Harrison relays a Berlin press report on the Japanese Cabinet's approval of a permanent food council.
subfiles.summary: Telegram No. 291: Harrison cites a Berlin paper on Japan's Cabinet approving a permanent Food Council to control food production and distribution.
subfiles.title: Telegram #291 from Harrison (Bern) on Cabinet Approval of Japanese Food Council
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs and Communications and Records

subfiles.about: Reports on Japanese efforts to achieve food autarky in Japan and occupied territories following the creation of the Food Council.
subfiles.summary: Berlin press report (January 1943) on Japan's new Food Council and its intensive push for agricultural and dietary self-sufficiency across occupied areas.
subfiles.title: Press Report on Japanese Food Autarky Efforts and the Food Council
